properties.description:
AUTHORED_BY now carries `roles` (list) and `authored_at` / `reviewed_at` / `approved_at`, in place of the single `role` + `acted_at` (schema/core.yaml). `DesignGraph::authored_by` MERGES: it reads what the (node, contributor) pair already holds, adds the role, sets that role's date, and writes the set back in canonical order so two writes in either order produce a byte-identical edge and the export does not churn. A role outside author/reviewer/approver is refused at the typed door (`AUTHORED_ROLES`), which is where the old schema enum's job moved; the MCP `authored_by` tool's `role` enum is generated from the same list.

WHY THE SHAPE AND NOT THE KEY: the store's identity for an edge is (graph, type, from, to); putting the role into the key would be a storage-format change for every store on disk (AGENTS.md's migration warning), and a second edge type would have rippled through ~330 references that name `role=approver` as the CALL. The set keeps the call surface intact and gives the two facts room inside one identity.

LEGACY, three ways: `authored_roles` / `edge_has_role` read the set OR the single `role` (default author), so an unmigrated store reads right; `migrate_authored_by_roles` rewrites legacy edges on every on-disk open (idempotent, one scan — nothing is stamped on a graph directory to key a one-shot migration); `import_graph` normalises a legacy export on the way in. A legacy `role` found BESIDE a set is dropped, not merged — an older binary's schema injects `role: author` by default on every write, and merging it would mint a phantom author.

THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT PATHS (acknowledge_gap_by, acknowledge_defect_by) now go through `authored_by` rather than building the edge by hand, so they merge too. The two readers that made the approver signature load-bearing (loop_status's assigned decisions, what_next's band 1) read the set. tools/check_intent_authority.py and smoke_mcp.py read the set and tolerate the legacy shape.

MEASURED on reflow2's own store at first open with the new binary: 842 AUTHORED_BY edges rewritten, 0 left in the legacy shape, 0 carrying both author and approver — the displaced authors are gone for good; what this guarantees is that no more are lost.
properties.name: A contributor's roles toward a node are a set that a write adds to, with a date per role
